images.title: One number fits the other
images.purpose: Show that the HCF of 6 and 18 is 6 because 6 is a factor of 18, and state the general form for n and 5n.
images.composition: Two horizontal bars drawn to scale sit in the centre, the short one above the long one, with two short caption lines below; generous white space.
exact_structure: Upper bar: one teal #0072B2 bar of length 6 units, labelled 6, left aligned with the lower bar.
Lower bar: one bar of length 18 units divided by thin dark lines into exactly 3 equal amber #E69F00 blocks, each the same length as the teal bar, labelled 18.
The text 6 × 3 = 18 to the right of the lower bar.
Caption line 1 below, in reddish purple #CC79A7: HCF of 6 and 18 is 6.
Caption line 2 below it, in dark text: HCF of n and 5n is n.
labels: HCF of n and 5n is n
rejection: other than exactly 3 equal blocks in the 18 bar, or blocks not matching the 6 bar
bars not drawn to the 6 to 18 scale
images.takeaway: When one number is a factor of the other, the smaller number is their HCF.
images.description: A bar of 6 above a bar of 18 split into three blocks of 6, with captions HCF of 6 and 18 is 6 and HCF of n and 5n is n.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on pairs whose HCF is one of the numbers.
images.teaching_notes: Check that the short bar fits the long bar exactly a whole number of times; then the short bar's number is the HCF.

image_decisions.why: Two scaled bars show directly why a factor of the other number is the HCF.
